newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JUNE 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JUNE 17.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Greek telecoms organisation OTE's second public share offer has brought the state upwards of 349 billion drachmas, with the interest demonstrated by Greek and foreign investors a first for the Greek capital market. Institutional investors from the US, Britain and other international markets placed orders for 82 million shares.

--A Supreme Court ruling on the payment of compound interest that has reversed a two-decade old precedent has been referred to the full bench of the court. The ruling says that banks can only impose compound interest on debtors' loans if they agree on the manner of repayment.

--Service-related firms took off and industry consolidated in the 1992-1996 period in Greece, according to a new survey. In terms of capital spent on new firms in various sectors, service led with industry second, and commerce and tourism bringing up the rear.

--Wages and remuneration and their role in inflation and competitiveness in the Greek economy are the focus of concern from the government and the Bank of Greece. A special committee will hand over its report on possible courses for the government's incomes policy this week. The report, sources say, calls for stricter wage increases for the next few years to contain inflation and deficits.
--The unprecedented demand for OTE shares has set a new rhythm for the Greek capital market and will provide a role model for planned share offers for other public enterprises and organisations.

--The tax department will impose lower fines and punishments following the conclusion that massive fines work against the collection of the same. The new philosophy is enshrined in a bill to be submitted to Parliament this week.
--Sources at the development ministry estimate that CPI-inflation for June will stabilise at 5.4 percent and may even slightly increase.

--Public transport systems in Athens returned a deficit of 720 billion drachmas in 1996. Increased passenger numbers was mismatched with lower fares, increased operating costs and interest repayments. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
